source.compiler: The game's own team files: the six national team files (TEAM.080 to 085) and the seven league files (TEAM.008 England, 013 France, 014 Germany, 020 Italy, 025 Holland, 029 Portugal, 035 Spain), as the SWOS United community server keeps them for its tools (cern.swos.eu/data/amiga/9697), read by scripts/lib/swos-files.mjs
source.provenance: SWOS 96/97 as released in 1996, the server's only 96/97 edition (9697). Until 2026-11-13 this season was read from Whiteulver's database of the game (xflea's spreadsheet v1.1, as keyser1884's SWOS-MCP holds it: swos_database.db, commit ac15d74), nations only, because that database names 688 full names at two clubs across all its divisions (Bierhoff at Ascoli and Udinese); the game's seven league files name 20 at two top-division clubs, mostly namesakes (Emerson at Middlesbrough, St. Pauli and Belenenses), and Thomas Wolter twice at Werder Bremen, as SWOS 94/95's and 95/96's files do, and each club keeps its own sixteen. Read from these files, every nation keeps the database build's strength and squad size, and 127 of the 133 with players the same eleven: two names keep the apostrophe the database dropped (D'Silva of India, Shar'aa of Jordan), and four ties between players of one price step fall to the files' order (Brazil fields Leonardo, not Dunga). Steps 0 and 49 are read as that database stores them (0 as 1, 49 as 48): 51 players, Shearer and Maldini at 49, listed in the audit. A SWOS United thread (2021) says some minor nations' squads and nationalities in the game predate 1996.
